title: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & SDLC: Security & Compliance Operational Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operational requirements and procedures for: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging and log retention, data residency and retention policies, Secure Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) requirements, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence collection workflows, and handling risk & exceptions. It is intended for engineering, security, and compliance teams who implement, operate, and validate controls.

Goals
- Ensure least-privilege access across cloud, control plane, and customer-facing systems.
- Provide tamper-evident, centralized audit logging with clear retention and access rules.
- Meet customer and regulatory residency/retention commitments.
- Embed security gates into the SDLC to prevent regressions and evidence generation for audits.
- Formalize incident response actions that preserve forensic evidence and compliance obligations.
- Define an auditable, timely exception and risk acceptance process.

Owner and Scope
- Owner: Security (policy and control design) and Eng-SRE (operational enforcement).
- Scope: All Redwood-managed control plane, hosting APIs, internal admin consoles, dedicated and private deployment orchestration layers, and CI/CD pipelines.

1) RBAC and Authentication

Summary
We enforce role-based access control across all surfaces (cloud consoles, infra orchestration, Redwood Console, CI/CD, and sensitive storage). RBAC policies are declarative, reviewed, and tracked in source control.

Key requirements
- Principle of least privilege applied to all roles. Default roles: system-admin, infra-engineer, svc-account, developer, support-analyst, auditor.
- All human access requires SSO via Okta with MFA (hardware token for admins).
- Service accounts must be short-lived (recommended <= 30 days) or use workload identity (OIDC) with scoped audiences.
- Just-in-time (JIT) elevation for high-privilege actions where practical.
- Access reviews: quarterly for all privileged roles; owners must attest in the access registry.

Ownership and workflows
1. Role definition: Security defines canonical role templates in git: infra/roles/*.yaml.
2. Provisioning requests: via the Access Request ticketing template (see Access Request Procedure).
3. Approval: Role owner + manager sign-off required for new privileged assignments.
4. Deprovisioning: Onboarding/offboarding hooks in HR system trigger IAM revocation within 24 hours for terminated employees.

Example RBAC snippet (declarative role template)
- name: support-analyst
  permissions:
  - read:customer-metadata
  - list:jobs
  - create:incidents
  notes: "No direct access to PII or audit-log export."

2) Audit Logging

Summary
Audit logs must be centralized, immutable, and searchable for forensic, compliance, and operational uses. Logging pipelines must support role-based access to logs and must retain integrity guarantees.

Minimum events to capture
- Admin console actions (user create/delete, role changes, policy changes).
- CI/CD pipeline runs (who triggered, commit SHA, artifacts, deploy targets).
- API authentication and authorization failures (401/403), token issuance and revocation events.
- Data access to customer-controlled storage and any access to PII or customer-supplied workloads in private deployments.
- System events related to cryptographic key management (KMS/HSM operations with metadata).

Logging architecture
- Collection: Fluentd/Vector agents on services forward to a centralized cluster (GCP Stackdriver / BigQuery or AWS CloudWatch -> S3 bucket depending on environment).
- Processing: Logs are enriched with request_id, user_id, role, region, and model_id.
- Storage: Immutable, write-once S3 buckets or cloud equivalent with object lock for regulated customers.
- Search & analytics: SIEM (Splunk/Elastic) with RBAC for auditors.

Retention and retention policy table
| Data type | Retention (default) | Rationale | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Authentication & Authorization events | 2 years | Forensics & compliance | Security |
| Admin console audit trails | 7 years (enterprise) / 2 years (standard) | Contractual & legal | Security / Legal |
| CI/CD build logs | 1 year | Reproducibility & investigation | Eng-Platform |
| Application request logs (non-PII) | 90 days | Cost / operations | Eng-SRE |
| PII access events | 7 years | Regulatory obligations | Security / Legal |

Access to logs
- Audit logs are accessed via SIEM consoles with a separate auditor role.
- Log exports for investigations require an approved ticket and are logged in the evidence registry.

Integrity controls
- Object locking / WORM storage or signed log bundles for high-sensitivity logs.
- Periodic checksum verification (weekly) and retention validation.

3) Data Residency & Retention

Policy summary
- Data classification: customer_data, telemetry, operational_metadata, logs. Each class has residency and retention profiles documented in the Data Classification matrix.
- Customer-data residency: Customers can choose region(s) (US, EU, APAC). For Private deployments, customer-managed regions apply.
- Cross-border transfers: Only allowed when contractually permitted; must be logged and approved by Legal.

Retention defaults
- Customer data (active): retained until customer deletion request or contract expiry.
- Backups: encrypted, retained for 90 days by default, unless customer requests longer.
- Telemetry/metrics: 13 months aggregated, raw event windows depend on cost tier.

Encryption & key management
- Data at rest: AES-256 for all storage.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys (CMKs) supported for Dedicated/Private; otherwise Redwood-managed keys with quarterly rotation.
- Key access: KMS admin role restricted to Security and SRE on a need-to-know basis.

Residency controls and verification
- Deployment manifests include region tags and are validated by pre-deploy compliance checks in CI.
- Periodic (quarterly) residency audits: verify metadata, snapshots, and backups match claimed regions.

4) Secure SDLC Requirements

Security gates in pipeline
1. Pre-commit: linters and secret-scan (git-secrets, truffleHog).
2. Pull Request: automatic SAST scan and dependency vulnerability check; failing high/critical breaks merge.
3. Pre-deploy: IaC plan review with policy-as-code (Open Policy Agent) validating network and data residency constraints.
4. Canary & progressive rollout: feature flags + canary threshold monitoring for anomaly detection.

Developer responsibilities
- All new services must include threat model, data flow diagram, and a test plan with privacy considerations.
- Security review required for services handling customer_data or PII (formal checklist sign-off).

Release evidence and artifact retention
- Signed SBOMs, SAST/SCA reports, and test results must be stored in the compliance evidence registry for at least 2 years (or per contractual obligation).

5) Incident Response - Security Procedures

High level
This section describes the security-focused incident response procedure to be followed alongside the standard incident management playbooks (oncall_and_incident_response). It focuses on preserving evidence, minimizing blast radius, and communicating with stakeholders including Legal and Customer Success when required.

Incident classification (examples)
- Sev-1: Data exfiltration of customer_data, active compromise of control plane.
- Sev-2: Unauthorized admin-level access without confirmed exfiltration.
- Sev-3: Service disruption with potential for data exposure.

Immediate steps (first 60 minutes)
1. Triage: Confirm scope and classification.
2. Evidence preservation: Snapshot affected instances, preserve memory if compromise suspected, and freeze relevant logs (set retention and export).
3. Containment: Revoke compromised credentials, rotate affected keys, and enact network ACL changes or isolate services.
4. Communication: Notify Security oncall, Eng-SRE, Legal, and the CEO if Sev-1.

Forensics and investigation
- Forensics lead to coordinate with Eng-SRE to collect disk snapshots, memory images (if allowed by customer contract), and export signed log bundles.
- All forensic artifacts must be hashed (SHA-256), stored in evidence S3 with object lock, and recorded in the incident evidence tracker.

Customer & regulatory notification
- Follow the notification timelines in the Incident Notification Matrix. For data breaches involving customer_data, Legal will assess regulatory timelines (EU GDPR 72-hour window).

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Purpose
To ensure auditable artifacts are produced, tracked, and retained to satisfy internal audits, SOC2/ISO assessments, and customer due diligence.

Evidence registry & templates
- Central registry: secure S3 bucket + metadata DB (read-only for auditors).
- Evidence types: policy attestations, access review logs, signed SBOMs, SCA/SAST reports, penetration test reports, incident evidence bundles, architecture diagrams, and contractually required residency attestations.

Workflow (typical)
1. Evidence produced by owner (e.g., Eng-Platform) with metadata (owner, date, retention, tags).
2. Submit via compliance upload tooling which validates schema and computes hash.
3. Security reviews and marks evidence as accepted or requests remediation.
4. Evidence retention automated by lifecycle policies; deletion requires a documented retention exception.

Audit response steps
- On audit request, Security assembles a package per auditor checklist in <3 business days for standard requests; SLA adjustable for enterprise customers with negotiated timelines.

7) Risk & Exceptions

Exception process
- Any deviation from policy must be submitted as a Risk & Exception request in the Risk Registry (git + ticket).
- Required fields: description, affected systems, mitigation controls, compensating controls, estimated duration, owner, and business justification.
- Review cycle: Security triage -> Risk Committee (monthly) -> Final approval by CISO for >90-day exceptions or high-risk items.

Acceptance criteria
- Acceptable residual risk score <= threshold defined in Risk Scoring rubric. High-risk requests must include a rollback/mitigation timeline and an expiration date.

Expiration & renewal
- Exceptions auto-escalate 14 days before expiry. Renewal requires re-evaluation and evidence of reduced risk.

Appendices
A. Access Request Procedure (step-by-step)
1. Open Access Request template in the Ticketing system.
2. Provide justification, requested role, and duration.
3. Notify approvers: role owner and manager.
4. Security performs a risk check and finalizes provisioning.

B. Incident Evidence Packaging Checklist
- Hash of artifact (SHA-256)
- Collection time (UTC)
- Collector name and role
- Chain of custody log
- Signed authorization for export (if customer-managed)

C. Sample OPA policy (pseudo)
package residency

allow {
  input.deployment.region in ["us-west1", "us-east1", "europe-west1"]
  input.customer_residency == input.deployment.region
}

D. Contacts & escalation matrix
- Security oncall: pager + Slack #security-oncall (see rota)
- CISO: ciso@redwood.ai
- Legal (Privacy): privacy-legal@redwood.ai
- Eng-SRE lead: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai
